belongs_to: Puzzle! 'Try This' 1 - three different fractional units that add up to 1: 'This explains why there is only one solution to the above problem' (circle figure above 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1; later referred to as 'divide a circle into parts like in the figure above')
description: One circle divided into 6 equal sectors by 3 diameters (one vertical, the other two tilted 30 degrees above and below the horizontal, so the cuts run from the centre to the 12, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 o'clock positions on the rim). The 6 sectors are equal (60 degrees each) and separated by thin dark lines. Colouring, going clockwise from 12 o'clock: sector 1 (12 to 2 o'clock, top right) dark blue/indigo = 1 sector; sectors 2 and 3 (2 to 4 o'clock right side, and 4 to 6 o'clock bottom right) orange = 2 sectors; sectors 4, 5 and 6 (6 to 8 o'clock bottom left, 8 to 10 o'clock left, 10 to 12 o'clock top left) green = 3 sectors. So green is 3 of 6 = 1/2 of the circle, orange is 2 of 6 = 1/3, blue is 1 of 6 = 1/6. Centred under the circle, as a caption with no colour coding, is the equation 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1 (three stacked fractions then = 1). No other labels, numbers or key on the circle itself.
